THE BATTLES TO BIKES STORY:

 

For over 20 years, Jim Yurek (The Bike Lab owner) served his local western Pennsylvania communities as a police officer and in those decades, time and again he interacted with United States veterans in need. At the point he intercepted these American heroes, they were often deep in the throes of trauma, anguish and the feeling that America had forgotten about them. Many of these veterans struggled with mental illness, substance abuse, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder and physical injuries related to military combat. Following his retirement from law enforcement, Jim made a significant career change in 2021 and opened The Bike Lab.

 
Jim soon made friends with Drew, an Army veteran and bike enthusiast, and through the sharing of his harrowing military stories, spurred Jim’s quest to find a way to serve local veterans through The Bike Lab. The idea of Battles to Bikes was born. 


In the fall of 2021, a small but passionate group joined forces as the Board of Directors for Battles to Bikes. The five-member Board is composed of business leaders, bike enthusiasts and local community members with a shared vision to serve the veterans of western Pennsylvania. One of the Board members is also an Army veteran. Drew serves as a Board Advisor.

 
In October 2022, Battles to Bikes was designated a 501c3 non-profit organization by the Internal Revenue Service. Starting out slow as many non-profits do, the initial funds of Battles to Bikes were raised through small raffles and a 62-mile paid-registration group bike ride event on the Great Allegheny Passage (GAP) in July 2022. Using an anonymous application process, Battles to Bikes – supported by The Bike Lab – was able to gift its first mountain bike, a Giant, to a local veteran on Saturday, November 12, 2022 in honor of Veterans Day.

 
In May 2023, Battles to Bikes presented a new Giant Cypress to our friends at Pittsburgh Warriors, a military service-connected hockey team for disabled veterans. Pittsburgh Warriors gifted the bicycle to veteran / Pittsburgh Warriors participant, Josh, who used his new rig to train for and participant in the July 2023 Healing Ride, a GAP trail ride from Pittsburgh to Washington, D.C. Since the inception of Battles to Bikes, we have gifted over 12 bicycles to local veterans.

 
Be sure to watch the Battles to Bikes’ Facebook page for fundraising events and group rides!

EventName: Annual Deborah Barisch Memorial Kings Gap Time Trial
EventNotes:
Join us for a timed ascent of one of the greater Harrisburg area's most popular climbs!

Back this year is the Kings Gap TT/Hill Climb, in memorial of Deborah Barisch, whom we unexpectedly lost in February of 2019. Deb was a pillar of her community and will be forever missed by those who knew her. Please join us in memorializing her memory at this event. A portion of the proceeds of this event will be donated to the Friends of Kings Gap organization.

 

Kings Gap State Park features a winding 4-mile paved road that climbs at an average gradient of 5%. It is almost entirely shaded corridor and will be closed to vehiclar traffic during the race. This has made it a favorite climb for cyclists all over the Cumberland Valley. Check out the Deborah Barisch Memorial Kings Gap TT Strava Segment. 

 

Day-of registration is available for an additional $10.00.

All event services including parking, check-in/registration, restrooms, etc. will be at the top of the mountain, adjacent to the mansion. 

Here are a couple of critical reminders that we are asking you all to address prior to showing up:

  • Please DO NOT come to the race if you have been sick in the past 14 days, run a fever, or not felt well.  
  • Maintain 6 feet of social distance from others as much as possible off the bike. 
  • Clean your hands before eating, touching your face, etc. Hand sanitizer is very effective and easily transported. 
  • Clean equipment after the ride. Disinfectant wipes, soap and water, 70% isopropyl alcohol all work.

Our start/finish gantry crosses the road.  DO NOT DRIVE UNDERNEATH THE GANTRY.  You will be held liable for any damages to your property or ours.

EventName: Randy Nixon's CrosstoberFest at Frey's Farm
EventNotes:
Randy Nixon's CrosstoberFest at Frey's Technical Guide 2026

In Memory of Randy Nixon: 

  

 

All USA Cycling Cyclocross rules apply.

  • Held under USA Cycling permit.
  • For age-graded races, Racing Age is defined as your age on December 31, 2027.
  • Mountain bikes are allowed, but bar ends are NOT permitted and must be removed.
  • There will be 1 double pit on the course.
  • Event will be held rain or shine.

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  

All registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $25 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for day-of registration by 8:30pm on Friday;  check-in will open by 8:30 AM on the day of the event.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

U19 Men & Women may race in any class they qualify for by Cyclocross category, but remain eligible for the Junior entry fee.  U19 Men and Women ONLY may use coupon code CFX2026_JRS at checkout to receive the Junior pricing; for race day entry, the day-of surcharge will be applied as appropriate.  Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry in all races other than Li'l Belgians.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

The Venue: 

Crosstoberfest is located at Frey's Farm which is Frederick County's first operational farm brewery, located in Mount Airy, Maryland. Frey's was established in 2012 by Air Force vet, Adam Frey, and their beautiful tasting room opened in early 2019 inside a fully-renovated, 200-year-old bank barn. NO outside alcohol permitted at the event venue.  

The Hosts:

Bluemont Connection was founded in 2016 by a group of four friends who wanted to race cyclocross together. Since then, the team has grown to more than 20 members who love gravel adventure, as well as CX. Bluemont hosts the popular Tuesday Towpath ride from Georgetown each week and also puts on B3 in Lost River, WV each spring.

Sportif Coaching Group/AVC is a Mid-Atlantic based cycling club with teams based in Maryland and Virginia.  Members of the team participate in nearly all disciplines of cycling but the majority are focused on Cyclocross. The club is sponsored by Sportif Coaching Group, Hunts End Remodeling, Patapsco Bicycles, Shulman/Rogers, and Element Sports.

Neutral Support by Patapsco Bicycles

 

Electronic Chip Timing by Insight Timing Services

 

Warmups:  The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 15 minutes prior to each event. Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. DQ & forfeiture of entry fee will result.

Novice Racer Guided Course Preview:  This on-bike preview is for Novice racers who will be competing in the 12:00pm Novice race block. You will be guided through the race course by experienced local racers and coaches. This begins promptly at 10:30am at the Staging Grid. 

Course Description:  Located at Frey's Farm in Mount Airy, Maryland, our course includes grass, gravel, hard-pack dirt, soft soil, and various barriers. The Brewery is a scenic venue for a race and offers wonderful spectating opportunities, with nearly the entire course visible from the Brewery's spacious deck.

Course Preview:  The course will be open for preview starting at 8:00am until just before the first race and then briefly between races. 

Start Line Protocol:  Racers must report to the holding pen adjacent to the starting grid for staging 15 minutes before the start of their race. 

Categories listed with the same start time may start up to 30 second apart at the discretion of the Race Director and Chief Official. 

Staging:  All races will reserve up to 1 spot in the first row and up to 1 spot in the second row, which are to be used for promoters' discretion call-ups. Otherwise staging for riders registered prior to the close of early registration is based on a rider's Crossresults Rankings as of 9:30am on Friday, September 25 2026. If multiple pre-registered riders in the same race have the same Crossresults Ranking those riders will additionally be staged based on their registration date & time. Riders who register after the close of early registration at 8:30am on Friday, September 25 2026 will be staged after the riders who registered early based on the their order of check-in on race day. 

Lapped Riders: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders. Per USA Cycling Rule 4G.: Lapped riders must yield the course to overtaking riders as quickly, efficiently and as safely as possible. Overtaking riders shall announce themselves sufficiently in advance of attempting to pass. Both overtaking and lapped riders shall be jointly responsible for a safe pass.

Pit:  There will be one double-sided pit on the course. Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others. 

Field Limits:  For the races with combined fields the 150 field limit is for the COMBINED field, not for each individual field. BikeReg has been set up so that once the limit has been reached for the combined field registration will close for each of the individual fields within the combined field.

Podiums and results reporting: 

All podiums will feature the top 5 finishers eligible for that specific podium. Podiums will be held as soon as possible following the end of the 15-minute protest period for results. 

The following races will have multiple podiums:

Masters 50+/60+/70+ Open. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 50+, 60+, and 70+ finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Masters 40+/50+ Cat. 4/Novice. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 40+ and 50+ finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Junior 11/12 & 13/14 Men. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 11/12 and 13/14 finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Junior 11/12 & 13/14 Women. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 11/12 and 13/14 finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Junior 9-10 Men & Women. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 9-10 men and 9-10 women finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Master Women 40+/50+/60+/70+ Open. This race will have separate podiums for the top five 40+, 50+, 60+, and 70+ finishers but will be posted to USA Cycling and Crossresults as a consolidated set of results.

Prizes:

All cash and prizes will be awarded based on the information listed above.

Races listed as Prizes/3 will pay merchandise prizes to the top 3 finishers.

Races listed as Prizes/5 will award merchandise prizes to the top 5 finishers for each of that race's podiums.

Races listed as Medals/3 will award medals to the top 3 finishers.

Races listed as Medals/3 + Prizes/3 will award medals and merchandise prizes to the top 3 finishers.

Races listed as Medals/3 + Prizes/5 will award medals to the top 3 finishers and merchandise prizes to the top 5 finishers for each of that race's podiums

Common Courtesy: Please be respectful of the environment and its inhabitants. We are guests of the brewery and there will be other customers present on race day. We would like to remind everyone that we all have a responsibility to leave the race course cleaner than we found it. All refuse should be discarded into appropriate containers. Any rider found illegally discarding objects on the brewery grounds, the roads leading to and from the race course, and/or the race course itself will be dealt with accordingly (see USA Cycling Rule 3B10, which states in part – ‘All riders must respect nature and the environment throughout the course and not to pollute the site. Riders may not discard materials that are not biodegradable; they may pass or throw such material in designated green zones or to support personnel in places far from any bystanders. It is strictly forbidden to throw waste directly onto the course or outside the areas as noted above [fine and/or disqualification for littering].'. Trash containers will be available for rider’s to use at registration.

Sportsmanlike Conduct:  The Chief Referee and Race Director expect ALL spectators and riders to act like responsible adults. Use of profanity and blatant unsportsmanlike conduct will not be tolerated. This is a family-friendly event and we are not the only people at the venue so please be courteous to venue patrons and staff.

Other Rules:  No outside alcohol permitted at the venue. Dogs must be kept on leash at all times. 

For more information and questions, please email:  glennpstevens@gmail.com

As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race
 
OTHER NOTES:
· Helmets are required for all races.
· Please arrive early to check in. Check-in closes 30 minutes prior to start times.

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 7:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventNotes:
Thanks for signing up to volunteer at this month WeROK MTB Group ride!  Our start times change with the seasons—because the mountain rides best when it wants to. May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT.  We look forward to riding with you soon! 

 

Meeting Location: Lower Lot, Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132
 

Please come to the ride with your name written in big letters on masking tape.
 

Please arrive 30 minutes prior to ride start time so we can be ready when the participants arrive.
 

Upon arrival, please pick up a Yellow Vest and rest your bike by your group sign.  The riders will be looking for their groups by approaching the ride leaders/sweepers with Yellow Vest. Groups will be spread out, all leaving from the same field but in the small group you lead.

 

Things to remember:

  • Check your bike and bring a working mountain bike.
  • Bring a water bottle or water bladder pack.
  • Feel free to bring snacks and beverages of your choice for Post Ride Social gathering.


Thank you for volunteering!  Let's Ride Bikes!

#WeROK #beYoudoYouforYou #YouBelong

REGISTRATION NOTES: 

  • Online registration closes at 11:59PM on Friday prior to race day.
  • No refunds due to buyer's remorse/if you are unable to attend.
  • In the unfortunate event that we are forced to cancel the event due to COVID, inclement weather, or other circumstances beyond our control, the race director will seek to refund entry fees, but cannot refund BikeReg fees.

LICENSES: All races will be held under USA Cycling (USAC) permit. Riders without an annual USAC license will be required to purchase a 1-day license for $15. Renew your annual license online at http://www.usacycling.org/.

All USAC rules apply. Helmets must be worn at all times.

This is the ninth year of the Garnet Hill Grit Race and we look to have a great event.  We have some great trails and all races will start at the Outdoor Center but finish at the main lodge on the front lawn with the most beautiful view of Thirteenth lake.  After the race join us for a hearty meal with lots of great things to eat and drink.  We always have a great post race barbecue and local beer awaits all racers 21 and older.  Awards will follow the races and each racer will receive a Dri-Fit Unisex race t-shirt (Guaranteed to the first 150 racers).  We are looking forward a great day with lots of fun in a beautiful area.  Come on up and see all Garnet Hill has to offer.

Registration and shirt pick up will be from 8:30 to 9:30 at the Outdoor Center.  We look forward to seeing you all there
